source.snippet: When running any jobs, there is no way to pause, stop, and/or force stop an executing job. Currently, when a reconciliation job is running, you have to wait for it to finish before running another. Considering a reconciliation task can take hours on big libraries, which makes it painful to interrupt mid-way if you realize you made an error in your media profile configuration.

problem_statement: Users of self-hosted media library management tools lack the ability to pause, cancel, or force-stop long-running reconciliation jobs (which can take hours), forcing them to wait out erroneous runs before correcting configuration mistakes—wasting significant time.
target_segment: Power users and prosumers running self-hosted media management servers with large libraries (thousands of files)
notes: Buyer context: technically sophisticated self-hosted user with large media libraries; implicit time cost ('hours'). While this is a feature request on a free tool, it signals a gap in self-hosted media management job orchestration. Willingness to pay is moderate—this segment often prefers free tools but will pay for reliability/control. A managed cloud wrapper or a standalone job-control daemon for self-hosted media stacks could be monetizable.
